VC-ANA-004 shows processing error can dwarf instrument error, so 1% is the narrowest possible slice of 'analytical error'.

column4: Between-plot spatial variability of SOC CONCENTRATION, as the within-treatment within-site residual CV among replicate experimental units under identical management.
column15: DERIVED BY US from the primary dataset; see scripts/derive_g1_napeshm.py. Replicate EUs under identical management at one site differ only by spatial heterogeneity plus analytical error, so their residual variance is between-plot spatial variance. Estimated as the residual of a REML nested random-effects model, treatment nested within site, NOT by averaging per-treatment variances (unstable at 3-5 replicates, and it would weight a 3-replicate treatment equally with a 5-replicate one). Fitted on the LOG scale because within-treatment SD scales with treatment mean (log-log slope about 1.2, far from the 0 a constant-SD model assumes), so the natural parameter is a constant CV; CV = 100*sqrt(exp(sigma^2)-1). The interval is a 95% cluster bootstrap over SITES, the top-level independent unit - bootstrapping rows or treatments would ignore the nesting and give far too narrow an interval. 600/600 resamples converged and the bootstrap median (11.9%) sits essentially on the point estimate, so the estimator shows no material bias.
column19: UPPER BOUND, not a point estimate. NAPESHM has no lab duplicate, split-sample or QC columns, so analytical error cannot be separated from spatial error and the residual necessarily contains both (D-027). Since variances add, the true between-plot SPATIAL term is strictly smaller than 12.1%. Using VC-ANA-001's 1.25% analytical CV as a rough guide, the purely spatial part would be near sqrt(12.1^2 - 1.25^2) = 12.0% - so the inflation is small, but it is one-directional and must not be forgotten when this row feeds the Phase 5 audit (D-023).

column15: Same estimator, dataset and filters as VC-BPS-005; see scripts/derive_g1_napeshm.py. Stock computed per EU as b_soc/100 * bd_2mm * 15 * 100 = b_soc * bd_2mm * 15 Mg C/ha, so bulk density measurement error is propagated into this row and VC-BPS-005 is the cleaner of the two. sd_mg_c_ha = 11.1% * 26.39 = 2.93 Mg C/ha using the mean 0-15 cm stock of the SAME 212 EUs, so the reference stock is internal to the data rather than assumed by us - but the row is still flagged mean_dependent because the absolute figure moves if that mean is revised. COUNTER-INTUITIVE RESULT, DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPRESSED: stock CV (11.1%) is LOWER than concentration CV (12.1%) even though stock carries the extra bulk-density error. The cause is a within-treatment correlation between log SOC and log bulk density of -0.396: plots richer in organic matter are less dense, and at FIXED DEPTH the two partly cancel in the stock product. The negative covariance term (2*cov = -0.0028) outweighs the added density variance (+0.0012). This is a property of the fixed-depth convention, not a property of the soil.

column15: TWO assumptions, both consequential. (1) NORMALITY: the source reports mean absolute error, defined in its Eq. 3 as the mean of |SOC_initial - SOC_resampled| across sites. Assuming those paired differences are normal with zero mean, SD = MAE * sqrt(pi/2) = 5.1 * 1.2533 = 6.39 Mg C/ha, and likewise 7.5% -> 9.4%. (2) DIFFERENCE SCALE: 6.39 is the SD of the DIFFERENCE between two locations, not of a single observation. If the two locations are treated as independent draws from the same field, the per-observation relocation SD is 6.39 / sqrt(2) = 4.52 Mg C/ha. Phase 1 must state which of the two it is using; conflating them inflates or deflates MDC by a factor of sqrt(2). Not marked mean_dependent because the source reports both absolute and relative forms directly, so no assumed mean stock was needed.

The MAE-to-SD normality assumption of D-003 pushes the same way. Partially offset by the inclusion of analytical error, which inflates, but that term is far smaller.

Harmonisation assumption: we read the source's statement as saturation, i.e. relocation variance does not grow appreciably with distance over this range. This licenses modelling relocation error as distance-INDEPENDENT within a plot, which is the single most useful simplification available to Phase 1.

Saturation was demonstrated only out to about 7 m inside a 20 x 20 m plot; if error continues to grow beyond that, treating it as flat removes variance that is really there. The row is scoped to within-plot use precisely to bound this, but the direction is one-way.

column15: Recorded as a signed systematic bias and deliberately given NO harmonised SD (rule R9). The bias is CONDITIONAL on the bulk density trajectory: it is a function of the 1.5 -> 1.1 g/cm3 change, not a property of the sampling method alone. In the OSSE the bulk density change must therefore be swept as an EXOGENOUS scenario parameter, never taken from the carbon model's own output - see DECISIONS.md D-007.
column19: The prescribed bulk-density change of 1.5 to 1.1 g/cm3 is a 27% decrease, which sits at or just above the top of the 20-25% range of observed decreases the authors themselves cite as evidence of realism. Bias from the fixed-depth convention grows with the magnitude of the density change, so a scenario at the top of the observed range yields a bias at the top of the plausible range.
